examples.en: Our troops crossed the bridge first.
It was hard to tell friend from foe in the movie.
In the game, I took the role of supporting my teammates.
They say our side's losses were smaller than expected.
We have to send a signal to our side.
The more allies you have at work, the better.

explain: 아군은 '적군'과 짝을 이루는 말이에요. 전쟁이나 게임에서 같은 편을 가리키고, 일상에서 같은 편이라는 비유로 쓸 때도 있어요. 평소에는 '내 편'이라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '아군' is the pair of '적군' (enemy forces). It means your own side in a war or a game, and sometimes figuratively your allies. In daily talk people say '내 편' (on my side) more often.

en: good condition; school nursing care (as in the school nurse's office)

examples.en: My health condition is fine.
I got medicine from the school nurse.
The checkup result came out as good.
My stomach hurt, so I went to the school infirmary.
I was relieved to get a good rating.

examples.ko: 양호 등급이 나오면 다시 검사하지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: If you get a good grade, you don't need to be tested again.

explain: '양호'는 소리가 같은 두 단어예요. 학교의 '양호실', '양호 선생님'은 학생의 건강을 돌본다는 뜻(養護)이고, 검사 결과의 '양호'는 상태가 좋다는 뜻(良好)이에요. 지금 학교의 공식 이름은 '보건실'이지만 말할 때는 아직 양호실이라고 많이 해요.
explain_en: '양호' stands for two different words that sound the same. In '양호실' and '양호 선생님' it means looking after students' health (養護). On test or checkup results it means a good state (良好). The official school term is now '보건실', but people still often say '양호실'.

en: be in good condition; be satisfactory

examples.en: The patient's condition is better than yesterday.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 공기 질이 대체로 양호해요.
examples.en: The air quality in this area is generally good.
The test results were good.
I heard the company's finances are in good shape.
If the weather is good, we will leave tomorrow.
I graduated with good grades.

explain: '양호하다'는 보고서, 뉴스, 건강검진처럼 격식 있는 글과 말에서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '괜찮다', '좋다'를 훨씬 많이 말해요. 문제없이 괜찮은 정도라서 '아주 좋다'와는 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: '양호하다' belongs to reports, news and medical or checkup results. In everyday talk people say '괜찮다' or '좋다'. It means fine, with no problems, which is weaker than 'very good'.

examples.en: Aftershocks followed the big earthquake.

examples.ko: 여진은 며칠 동안 계속될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Aftershocks can continue for several days.

examples.ko: 여진 때문에 사람들이 집에 들어가지 못했어요.
examples.en: People couldn't go back home because of the aftershocks.
The news told people to watch out for aftershocks.

examples.ko: 지진이 끝난 줄 알았는데 여진에 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I thought the quake was over, but the aftershock startled me.

examples.ko: 여진이 올 때는 책상 아래로 들어가세요.
examples.en: When an aftershock comes, get under a desk.

explain: 큰 지진 다음에 오는 작은 지진만 '여진'이라고 불러요. 첫 지진은 '본진'이라고 해요. '여진이 이어지다', '여진이 계속되다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.example: 그 사건의 여진이 아직 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: The aftershocks of that incident still remain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지진이 아니어도 큰 사건이나 논란 뒤에 영향이 계속될 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when the effects of a big event or controversy linger on.

explain_en: Only the smaller quakes that follow a big earthquake are called '여진'. The first big one is the '본진'. It goes with verbs like '이어지다' and '계속되다'.

examples.en: In the old tale, the hero defeated the monster.
The hero in the game is a high-level character.

examples.ko: 그 마을에는 용감한 용사의 동상이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a statue of a brave warrior in that village.
The kids played holding sticks like heroic warriors.
Everyone welcomed the warriors who returned from the war.

examples.ko: 책 속 용사에게 마법의 검이 있었어요.
examples.en: The hero in the book had a magic sword.

explain: '용사'는 판타지 이야기, 게임, 옛이야기에서 용감하게 싸우는 사람을 가리켜요. 실제로 큰일을 한 사람은 '영웅'이라고 불러요. '참전 용사'는 실제 전쟁에 나간 사람이라 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '용사' is the brave fighter in fantasy stories, games and old tales. A real person who did something great is called a '영웅'. '참전 용사' (war veteran) appears often in the news.

examples.en: My friend broke a promise, so I resented him.
Please don't resent me.
The child went into the room resenting the parents.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어지고 제 자신을 원망하게 됐어요.
examples.en: After failing the exam, I ended up blaming myself.
Make your next plan instead of wasting time resenting.

examples.ko: 오래전에 헤어진 사람을 원망한 적은 없어요.
examples.en: I have never held a grudge against the person I parted from long ago.

explain: '원망하다'는 상대에게 섭섭하고 화난 마음을 오래 품는 거예요. '미워하다'는 싫은 감정 자체이고, '탓하다'는 잘못을 그 사람에게 돌리는 행동이에요. 보통 '누구를 원망하다'로 써요.
explain_en: '원망하다' is to carry hurt, angry feelings toward someone for a long time. '미워하다' is just the feeling of hating, and '탓하다' is the act of putting the blame on someone. It is used as '누구를 원망하다'.

examples.en: I entered a photo in the contest.

examples.ko: 이벤트에 응모하면 선물을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you enter the event, you can get a gift.
Please enter by the end of this month.

examples.ko: 응모한 사람 중에서 열 명을 뽑아요.
examples.en: They pick ten people from those who entered.
I lined up to enter the prize drawing.
My friend will enter a singing contest.

explain: '응모하다'는 공모전, 이벤트, 추첨처럼 정해진 모집에 신청한다는 느낌이에요. 회사나 학교에는 '지원하다', 단순히 이름을 올릴 때는 '신청하다'를 써요. '이벤트에 응모하다'가 가장 흔해요.
explain_en: '응모하다' is for entering a set call such as a contest, giveaway or drawing. For a company or school use '지원하다', and for simply signing up use '신청하다'. '이벤트에 응모하다' is the most common phrase.

examples.en: There is a big mansion on the hill.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 넓은 저택에서 살아요.
examples.en: The main character in the movie lives in a spacious mansion.

examples.ko: 이 저택은 백 년 전에 지어졌어요.
examples.en: This mansion was built a hundred years ago.
A rich man bought a mansion and decorated the garden.

examples.ko: 저택 안에는 방이 스무 개나 있대요.
examples.en: I heard there are twenty rooms inside the mansion.

examples.ko: 저택 주변에는 높은 담이 쳐져 있어요.
examples.en: A high wall surrounds the mansion.

explain: '저택'은 크고 고급스러운 집이에요. 주로 영화, 드라마, 뉴스에서 들어요. 내 집을 저택이라고 하면 농담처럼 들려요. 평범한 집은 그냥 '집'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '저택' is a large, grand house, mostly heard in films, dramas and the news. Calling your own house a '저택' sounds like a joke. An ordinary home is just a '집'.

examples.en: The police subdued the suspect.
They overpowered the other team and reached the final.
Some people take control of the mood from the start.

examples.ko: 경호원이 한 손으로 그 사람을 제압할 수 있어요.
examples.en: The bodyguard can subdue that person with one hand.

examples.ko: 아이를 제압하려고 소리치면 오히려 말을 안 들어요.
examples.en: If you shout to overpower a child, they listen even less.
The player overpowered his opponent and the crowd cheered.

explain: '제압하다'는 힘이나 기세로 상대가 움직이지 못하게 누르는 거예요. 시위나 불은 '진압하다', 경기에서 이기는 건 '이기다'가 더 자연스러워요. 눈빛이나 분위기로 사람들을 압도할 때도 써요.
explain_en: '제압하다' is to hold someone down with strength or presence so they can't act. For riots or fires use '진압하다', and for winning a game '이기다' sounds more natural. It can also describe overwhelming a room with a look or presence.

examples.en: The farmer sowed seed in spring.
If you choose good seed, the harvest increases.

examples.ko: 이 종자는 추위에 강해서 겨울에도 자라요.
examples.en: This variety is cold-hardy and grows even in winter.
Seed needs water to sprout.
The government developed a new rice variety.
The farmers' co-op sells seed and fertilizer together.

explain: '종자'는 농사에 쓰려고 고른 씨앗이나 품종이에요. 꽃씨나 수박씨는 일상에서 그냥 '씨'나 '씨앗'이라고 해요. '종자'는 농업 이야기나 뉴스 글에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '종자' is seed or a variety chosen for farming. For flower seeds or watermelon seeds people just say '씨' or '씨앗' in daily talk. '종자' shows up in farming talk and news writing.

examples.en: A hearing was held at the National Assembly.
The nominee answered questions at the hearing.

examples.ko: 청문회 장면이 하루 종일 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: Scenes from the hearing were on the news all day.
This hearing will be broadcast live.
The witness who came to the hearing changed his story.
Citizens who watched the hearing posted their opinions.

explain: '청문회'는 공직 후보자나 사건 관련자에게 질문하는 공식 자리로, 뉴스에서 자주 들어요. '인사 청문회'가 대표적이에요. 보통 '청문회가 열리다', '청문회를 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: A '청문회' is a formal session where officials ask questions of a candidate for a public post or people tied to an incident. You hear it in the news, most often as '인사 청문회'. It goes with '열리다' and '하다'.

examples.ko: 다리 같은 구조물은 안전 검사를 받아요.
examples.en: Structures like bridges get safety inspections.
A new structure appeared in the park.
The architect recalculated the height of the structure.

examples.ko: 철로 만든 구조물을 크레인이 들어 올렸어요.
examples.en: A crane lifted the structure made of steel.
We hung lights on the structure on the stage.

examples.ko: 해변에 설치된 구조물과 의자를 모두 치웠어요.
examples.en: We cleared away all the structures and chairs set up on the beach.

explain: '구조물'은 다리, 탑, 무대처럼 재료를 세우거나 쌓아 만든 큰 것을 뭉뚱그려 부르는 말이에요. 이름을 알면 '건물', '다리'처럼 정확히 말하고, 이름을 모르거나 여러 종류를 함께 말할 때 '구조물'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '구조물' is a general word for built things such as bridges, towers and stages. If you know what it is, you say '건물' or '다리'. '구조물' is for when you don't know the name or mean several kinds together.

examples.ko: 그는 대의를 위해 자기 이익을 포기했어요.
examples.en: He gave up his own interests for the greater cause.
Everyone agreed to the cause.
The greater cause matters more than small complaints.

examples.ko: 이 모임의 대의는 환경을 지키는 거예요.
examples.en: The cause of this group is protecting the environment.
It is hard to move people without a just cause.

examples.ko: 그 이야기는 대의보다 개인의 사연에 가까워요.
examples.en: That story is more about an individual than a cause.

explain: '대의'는 여러 사람이 함께 지켜야 한다고 믿는 큰 목적이에요. 보통 '대의를 위해', '대의에 따르다'로 써요. 비슷한 '명분'은 행동이 옳아 보이게 하는 이유예요. '대의명분'으로 묶어서도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: '대의' is a large purpose that many people believe they should uphold, as in '대의를 위해' (for the cause). The similar '명분' is the stated reason that makes an action look justified. They are often combined as '대의명분'.

examples.en: The bride wore a white veil.
Her face was faintly visible through the veil.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 사생활은 아직 베일에 싸여 있어요.
examples.en: That singer's private life is still shrouded in mystery.

examples.ko: 새 게임이 오늘 드디어 베일을 벗어요.
examples.en: The new game finally gets unveiled today.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 어머니가 신부의 베일을 바로잡아 줬어요.
examples.en: At the wedding, her mother straightened the bride's veil.

examples.ko: 창문에 얇은 베일 같은 커튼을 달았어요.
examples.en: I hung a thin, veil-like curtain on the window.

explain: '베일'은 얼굴이나 머리에 쓰는 얇은 천이에요. 결혼식 장면에서 볼 수 있고, 비유로 '아직 공개되지 않은 상태'를 말할 때도 많이 써요. 뉴스에서는 '베일에 싸이다', '베일을 벗다'가 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 회사의 새 계획은 아직 베일에 싸여 있어요.
phrases.en: The company's new plan is still shrouded in mystery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 일의 정체, 내용이 아직 알려지지 않았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the identity or contents of a person or matter are still unknown.

phrases.en: The new phone was unveiled today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감추어 둔 것이 처음 공개될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something kept hidden is revealed for the first time.

explain_en: '베일' is the thin cloth worn over the face or head, often seen at weddings. It is also widely used figuratively for something not yet made public. In news, '베일에 싸이다' and '베일을 벗다' come up often.

examples.en: The ship arrived at the dock.
They sell fish cheaply at the pier.
A truck loaded with cargo drove onto the wharf.
In the evening I took a walk along the pier.
The piers in this city are crowded with tourists.

examples.ko: 부두 근처에 맛있는 해산물 식당이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a good seafood restaurant near the dock.

explain: '부두'는 배를 대고 사람이 타고 내리거나 짐을 싣고 내리는 구체적인 자리예요. '항구'는 배가 드나드는 도시나 지역 전체의 느낌이고, '부두'는 그 안에서 배를 대는 곳이에요.
explain_en: '부두' is the specific spot where ships tie up and people or cargo get on and off. '항구' is the whole harbor town or area, and a '부두' is one of the places inside it.

examples.en: Our team conceded no points in the first half.
Defense is important to concede fewer points.
The players wobbled after the first goal against.

examples.ko: 그 투수는 한 경기 평균 실점이 낮아요.
examples.en: That pitcher gives up few runs per game on average.
We conceded only once, but the result was a loss.
The goalkeeper's mistake led to a goal against.

explain: '실점'은 경기에서 상대에게 점수를 내주는 거예요. 짝말은 '득점'이에요. '실점을 하다/줄이다/막다'처럼 써요. 시험에서 점수가 깎이는 건 '감점'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '실점' is giving up a point to the opponent in a game, and its pair is '득점' (scoring). It goes with '하다', '줄이다' and '막다'. Losing marks on a test is '감점'.

en: concede a point; give up a run

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 후반에 두 골을 실점했어요.
examples.en: Our team conceded two goals in the second half.
The defense wobbled and we ended up conceding.
Everyone fell back so as not to concede.
Every time we conceded, the coach called a timeout.
If you concede first, it is hard to turn the game around.
The pitcher who gave up runs in a row was replaced.

explain: '득점하다'와 짝을 이루는 스포츠 말이에요. 축구나 야구 중계에서 '실점 없이 막았다'처럼 자주 들려요. 일상에서는 '점수를 내주다'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: This is the sports pair of '득점하다' (to score). You often hear it in soccer and baseball broadcasts, as in '실점 없이 막았다'. In casual talk people also say '점수를 내주다'.

examples.en: The government decided to weaken the regulations.
The controversy grew after the rules were weakened.
That incident weakened trust in the company.

examples.ko: 너무 많은 규칙은 선수의 자율성을 약화할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Too many rules can weaken a player's autonomy.
Frequent quarrels weaken teamwork.

examples.ko: 새 규칙이 시험의 의미를 약화한다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think the new rule weakens the meaning of the exam.

explain: '약화하다'는 어떤 것을 일부러, 또는 결과적으로 약하게 만든다는 뜻으로 주로 써요. 저절로 약해질 때는 '약화되다'나 '약해지다'가 자연스러워요. 반대말은 '강화하다'예요. 뉴스, 글말에서 주로 나와요.
explain_en: '약화하다' mainly means making something weaker, on purpose or as a result. When something weakens by itself, '약화되다' or '약해지다' sounds more natural. Its opposite is '강화하다', and it appears mostly in news and writing.

en: go back and forth; make a round trip

examples.en: I go back and forth between home and work by bus every day.
I made a round trip between Seoul and Busan in a day.
The shuttle bus runs back and forth between the station and the school.

examples.ko: 차로 한 시간이면 왕복할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can make the round trip in an hour by car.
A round trip on foot takes about two hours.

examples.ko: 도서관을 왕복하는 길에 꽃이 많이 피었어요.
examples.en: Many flowers bloomed along the way to and from the library.

explain: '왕복'은 '편도'와 짝이에요. 표를 살 때 '왕복 표 주세요', '편도로 주세요'라고 말해요. 동사 '왕복하다'는 '오가다'보다 딱딱하고, 거리와 시간을 말할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: '왕복' is the pair of '편도' (one way); when buying tickets you say '왕복 표 주세요' or '편도로 주세요'. The verb '왕복하다' is stiffer than '오가다' and is often used when talking about distance and time.

en: be widely talked about; be the talk of the town

examples.en: That restaurant is the talk of the town for its taste.

examples.ko: 그 선생님에 대한 칭찬이 학교에 자자했어요.
examples.en: Praise for that teacher was all over the school.

examples.ko: 소문이 자자하던 가게에 드디어 가 봤어요.
examples.en: I finally visited the shop everyone had been talking about.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 헤어졌다는 소문이 자자한데 사실일까요?
examples.en: There's talk everywhere that the two broke up, but is it true?
They say that actor's popularity is huge overseas too.

examples.ko: 칭찬이 자자하면 누구나 한 번 가 보고 싶어져요.
examples.en: When the praise is everywhere, anyone wants to go once.

explain: '자자하다'는 '소문이 자자하다', '칭찬이 자자하다', '명성이 자자하다'처럼 소문, 평판과 관련된 말과만 붙어요. 좋은 소문에도 나쁜 소문에도 쓰지만 실제로는 칭찬이나 인기에 가장 많이 써요.
explain_en: '자자하다' only pairs with words about rumor or reputation, such as '소문이 자자하다', '칭찬이 자자하다' and '명성이 자자하다'. It works for both good and bad talk, but in practice it is used most for praise and popularity.

examples.en: An American governor visited Korea.
The governor announced a new plan at a press conference.

examples.ko: 그 도시는 주지사의 결정을 따를 거예요.
examples.en: That city will follow the governor's decision.
There is a student who sent a letter to the governor.

examples.ko: 새 주지사를 뽑는 선거가 다음 달에 있어요.
examples.en: The election to choose a new governor is next month.
The governor and the mayor attended the event together.

explain: '주지사'는 미국처럼 '주'가 있는 나라에서 그 주를 이끄는 사람이에요. 한국에는 '주'가 없어서 도를 이끄는 사람은 '도지사'라고 불러요. 외국 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: '주지사' is the head of a state in countries like the United States. Korea has no states, so the head of a province (도) is called a '도지사'. You hear '주지사' mostly in foreign news.

examples.en: Jobs were created as the new factory opened.

examples.ko: 이 사업으로 큰 이익이 창출될 거예요.
examples.en: This business will generate a big profit.
I learned about the process in which new value is created.
When jobs are created, young people come back to the city.

examples.ko: 기술 덕분에 수백 개의 새 직업이 창출되었어요.
examples.en: Hundreds of new occupations were created thanks to technology.
The revenue that was generated was reused in the region.

explain: '창출되다'는 거의 '일자리, 가치, 수익, 이익'과 함께 쓰는 뉴스와 경제 말이에요. 요리나 물건이 만들어졌다고 할 때는 쓰지 않아요. 능동형은 '창출하다'이고, 신문에서는 '일자리를 창출하다'가 가장 흔해요.
explain_en: '창출되다' is a news and economics word used almost only with things like jobs, value, revenue and profit. You don't use it for a dish or an object being made. The active form is '창출하다', and '일자리를 창출하다' is the most common phrase in newspapers.

examples.ko: 특급 열차는 작은 역에 서지 않아요.
examples.en: The express train doesn't stop at small stations.
That hotel's service is top class.
I sent this parcel by express mail.
A top-class chef cooked for us himself.

examples.ko: 한 선수가 특급 신인으로 불리고 있어요.
examples.en: One player is being called a top rookie.
If you request express delivery, it arrives tomorrow.

explain: '특급'은 가장 높은 등급이에요. 열차, 호텔, 배송처럼 등급이 나뉜 것에 많이 써요. 사람이나 실력에 쓰면 '최고 수준'이라는 칭찬이 돼요. '특급 호텔', '특급 배송', '특급 신인'이 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '특급' is the top grade. It is common for things that come in grades, such as trains, hotels and delivery. For a person or skill it works as high praise. '특급 호텔', '특급 배송' and '특급 신인' are common.

examples.en: Busan is a city with a large port.
There are many ships loaded with containers at the port.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 항만이 하루 동안 닫혔어요.
examples.en: The port was closed for a day because of the typhoon.
Port workers start working early in the morning.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 항만 시설을 새로 짓고 있어요.
examples.en: This country is building new port facilities.

examples.ko: 항만과 철도가 연결되어 물건을 빨리 옮겨요.
examples.en: With the port and railway connected, goods move quickly.

explain: '항만'은 배가 드나들고 짐을 싣고 내리는 시설을 통틀어 부르는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '항구'를 더 많이 말하고, '항만'은 뉴스나 경제 글에서 규모와 시설을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: '항만' covers the whole set of facilities where ships come in and cargo is loaded. In daily talk '항구' is more common, while '항만' appears in news and economic writing when scale and facilities matter.

examples.en: A hacker broke into the company's server.
The news said hacker attacks have increased.
He handles computers like a hacker.
I change my password often to keep hackers out.

examples.ko: 보안 회사는 해커에게 시스템을 시험해 보게 했어요.
examples.en: The security firm had a hacker test its system.
A hacker and a security expert had a discussion together.

explain: 한국어 뉴스에서 '해커'는 보통 남의 컴퓨터에 몰래 들어가 나쁜 일을 하는 사람으로 들려요. 컴퓨터를 잘 다루는 사람은 '개발자'나 '프로그래머'라고 해요. 좋은 목적으로 보안을 점검하는 사람은 '화이트 해커'라고 불러요.
explain_en: In Korean news '해커' usually sounds like someone who breaks into computers for bad purposes. Someone who is just good with computers is a '개발자' or '프로그래머'. A person who tests security for a good purpose is called a '화이트 해커'.

examples.ko: 이 상자는 모서리가 각져서 손이 아파요.
examples.en: This box has sharp corners and hurts my hand.
He has a face with a square jaw.
Angular stones are dangerous to throw.
I made it round, but one side came out angular.
A cup without sharp edges is comfortable in the hand.
I folded the paper at sharp angles and made a box.

explain: '각지다'는 둥글지 않고 모서리가 반듯하거나 뾰족한 모양이에요. '각진 얼굴, 턱, 어깨'처럼 사람의 모습에 많이 쓰고, 반대는 '둥글다'예요. '각진 어깨'는 어깨선이 곧고 넓어 보이는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '각지다' describes a shape with straight or sharp corners rather than a round one. It is common for people's looks, as in '각진 얼굴', '각진 턱' and '각진 어깨'. Its opposite is '둥글다'. A '각진 어깨' means a straight, broad shoulder line.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 올해 도루를 서른 개나 했어요.
examples.en: That player had thirty stolen bases this year.
The steal succeeded and the team moved ahead.

examples.ko: 도루 성공률이 높은 선수가 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: Players with a high steal success rate are popular.
The steal failed and the crowd sighed.
The player named stolen-base leader gave an interview.
As steal attempts grew, the games got faster.

explain: 야구 중계에서는 '도루 성공', '도루 실패', '도루왕'처럼 기록을 말할 때 많이 나와요. '득점', '타점'과 함께 기록 말로 알아 두면 좋아요. 야구를 모르는 사람에게는 잘 쓰지 않는 말이에요.
explain_en: In baseball broadcasts it appears when recording stats, as in '도루 성공', '도루 실패' and '도루왕'. It is good to learn it together with '득점' and '타점'. It is not a word used with people who don't follow baseball.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤 땅에 새싹이 돋았어요.
examples.en: Sprouts came out of the ground after the rain.
In spring new leaves sprout on every branch.
Goosebumps rose on my arm when the cold wind blew.
It's the age when pimples break out on your face.
Teeth have started to come in on the baby's gums.

examples.ko: 새싹이 돋으면 화분을 햇빛 아래 두세요.
examples.en: When sprouts come out, put the pot in the sunlight.

explain: '돋다'는 새싹, 소름, 여드름, 치아처럼 땅이나 피부 위로 솟아 나오는 것에 써요. '돋아요', '돋는'으로 활용하고 '돋아나다'도 비슷한 뜻이에요. 해가 떠오를 때는 보통 '뜨다'를 쓰고, '돋다'는 '해돋이' 같은 말에서 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I got goosebumps at the last scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무서울 때뿐 아니라 감동하거나 놀랐을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not only when scared but also when moved or amazed.

explain_en: 돋다 is for things that push up through the ground or skin, such as sprouts, goosebumps, pimples and teeth. It conjugates as 돋아요 and 돋는, and 돋아나다 is similar. For the sun rising people usually say 뜨다, and 돋 only shows up in words like 해돋이 (sunrise).

examples.en: The child had a seizure because of a fever.
He suddenly had a coughing fit.
The ER doctor examined the seizure patient.

examples.ko: 천식 발작이 올 때를 대비해 약을 가지고 다녀요.
examples.en: I carry medicine in case I have an asthma attack.
The seizure stopped after a few minutes.
The family, shocked by the sudden attack, called 119.

explain: '발작'은 병 때문에 갑자기 증상이 크게 나타나는 일이에요. '기침 발작', '천식 발작'처럼 병이나 증상 앞에 붙여 많이 써요. '발작을 일으키다'가 가장 흔한 짝이에요.
explain_en: '발작' is when a symptom suddenly flares up because of an illness. It is commonly attached to an illness or symptom, as in '기침 발작' and '천식 발작'. '발작을 일으키다' is the most common pairing.

examples.en: The car wouldn't start this morning.
I turned off the engine and got out of the car.
When you press the start button, the lights come on.

examples.ko: 시동이 꺼지는 바람에 길 한가운데서 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The engine died, so we stopped in the middle of the road.

examples.ko: 오토바이는 시동을 걸 때 소리가 커요.
examples.en: A motorcycle is loud when you start the engine.

examples.ko: 요즘 전기차는 시동 소리가 거의 없어요.
examples.en: Electric cars these days make almost no sound when starting.

explain: 차, 오토바이, 기계를 처음 움직일 때 '시동'이라고 해요. '시동을 걸다'와 '시동을 끄다'가 짝이고, 달리다가 멈추면 '시동이 꺼지다'라고 말해요. 일이나 계획을 본격적으로 시작할 때도 '시동을 걸다'를 비유로 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 새 사업이 이제 막 시동을 걸었어요.
phrases.en: The new business has just got going.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 계획을 본격적으로 시작할 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when a job or plan is properly starting.

explain_en: '시동' is starting a car, motorcycle or machine for the first time. '시동을 걸다' and '시동을 끄다' are a pair, and if it stalls while running you say '시동이 꺼지다'. '시동을 걸다' is also often used figuratively for properly starting a job or plan.

examples.ko: 한국에 와서 겨울이 춥다는 걸 실감했어요.
examples.en: I really felt how cold winter is after coming to Korea.
It still hasn't sunk in that I've graduated.
Even after hearing the news of my acceptance, it was hard to take in.

examples.ko: 물가가 오른 것을 장을 볼 때 실감해요.
examples.en: I feel prices going up when I go grocery shopping.

examples.ko: 직접 가 보면 이 도시의 크기를 실감할 거예요.
examples.en: If you go there yourself, you will feel how big this city is.

examples.ko: 아이를 키우며 부모님의 마음을 실감하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people truly feel their parents' hearts while raising a child.

explain: '실감하다'는 머리로 알던 일을 직접 겪고서 확 와닿을 때 써요. 부정은 '실감하지 못하다'와 '실감이 안 나다' 둘 다 자주 말해요. 믿기지 않는 좋은 일이 생겼을 때 '실감이 안 나요'라는 말이 특히 흔해요.
explain_en: '실감하다' is used when something you knew in your head hits home after you experience it. The negative is said both as '실감하지 못하다' and '실감이 안 나다'. When something unbelievably good happens, '실감이 안 나요' is especially common.

examples.en: An elder of the academic world gave advice to juniors.
That actor is called a veteran of the film world.

examples.ko: 원로 가수의 공연에 많은 사람이 모였어요.
examples.en: Many people gathered for the veteran singer's concert.
I learned a lot listening to the elders' stories.

examples.ko: 우리 마을 원로께서 행사를 열어 주셨어요.
examples.en: An elder of our village held the event for us.
A veteran and a newcomer stood on stage together.

explain: '원로'는 한 분야에서 오래 일하고 존경받는 어른이에요. 보통 '원로 배우', '원로 가수', '원로 학자'처럼 직업 앞에 붙여요. 나이만 많은 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: '원로' is a respected senior figure with a long career in a field. It is usually put before a job, as in '원로 배우' or '원로 학자'. It isn't used for someone who is merely old.

examples.en: This book is exactly what beginners need.
Now is precisely the time to start.
Health is the greatest asset of all.
Promises, above all, are what you must keep.
Hangul is truly Korea's pride.
My classmates are truly the best team.

explain: '이야말로'는 여러 가운데 '바로 이것'이라고 강조하는 조사예요. 받침이 있는 말 뒤에는 '이야말로', 없는 말 뒤에는 '야말로'를 써요: '지금이야말로', '너야말로'. 상대의 인사를 받아서 '저야말로요'라고 하면 '오히려 제가 그래요'라는 대답이 돼요.
explain_en: '이야말로' is a particle that stresses 'this very one' among many. After a final consonant use '이야말로', and after a vowel use '야말로', as in '지금이야말로' and '너야말로'. In reply to someone, '저야말로요' means 'if anything, it's me'.

examples.en: The police rescued the hostage safely.
The people who had been held hostage were released.

examples.ko: 인질 사건이 나서 뉴스가 계속 나왔어요.
examples.en: A hostage incident happened and the news kept covering it.
My heart broke because my family became hostages.
A hostage negotiation expert arrived at the scene.
They say all the hostages are safe.

explain: '인질'은 주로 뉴스와 영화에서 들어요. '인질로 잡다/잡히다', '인질을 풀어 주다/구출하다'처럼 써요. 일상에서 비유로 '볼모'를 쓰기도 하지만 '인질'이 훨씬 흔해요.
explain_en: '인질' is mostly heard in news and films. It goes with '인질로 잡다/잡히다' and '인질을 풀어 주다/구출하다'. '볼모' also exists as a figurative word, but '인질' is much more common.
